title: Cut redundant positions and spending at the intelligence director's office
proposal: The text recommends that the President direct the Director of National Intelligence (DNI) to cut redundant positions and spending while giving the DNI power to drive changes across intelligence agencies.
quote: a desire to slash redundant positions and expenditures while simultaneously giving the DNI the authority to drive necessary changes

title: Amend Executive Order 12333 on how intelligence agencies operate
proposal: The text recommends revising Executive Order 12333, the main presidential order guiding intelligence agencies, to address new threats such as cyber attacks, China and Russia, instead of seeking new legislation.
quote: Executive Order 12333 should be amended to take account of the changing landscape of threats and improve the functional aspects

title: Define government cyber roles in the intelligence executive order
proposal: The text recommends that the revised order clearly set out the roles of the various federal cyber missions, including the National Cyber Director's office, while protecting Americans' privacy.
quote: The amended order should clearly delineate the roles and responsibilities of the various U.S. government cyber missions

title: Decide the NSA's split role between strategic and battlefield support
proposal: The text recommends that the revised order consider how DOD cyber agencies, especially the NSA, should divide support between national leaders and the military, alongside reviews of its "dual-hat" leadership.
quote: The order should consider stipulating what to do with DOD cyber agencies, most notably the NSA

title: Give the DNI more control over the intelligence budget
proposal: The text recommends strengthening the DNI's power to oversee the National Intelligence Program budget, including moving money and staff to higher priorities within limits set by Congress.
quote: Enhance the DNI’ s role in overseeing execution of the National Intelligence Program budget under the President’ s authority.

title: Strengthen open-source intelligence and avoid duplicating private firms
proposal: The text recommends that intelligence agencies avoid copying work the private sector already does well with public information, and that the DNI may name the deputy DNI to lead this effort.
quote: the DNI should appoint the Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence (PDDNI) as chairman to prioritize and promote accountability

title: Enforce faster security clearance processing across agencies
proposal: The text recommends that the DNI, who oversees security clearances, force agencies to carry out clearance reforms and honor each other's clearances within 48 hours.
quote: As executive agent for security clearances, the DNI must require results from agencies that resist implementation, enforce the 48-hour reciprocity guidance

title: Move the Security Services Directorate from NCSC to ODNI
proposal: The text suggests that moving the Security Services Directorate out of the National Counterintelligence and Security Center and into the main DNI office, with higher status, may be needed.
quote: including moving the Security Services Directorate from NCSC to ODNI with elevated status, may be necessary

title: Share more intelligence with Commerce to counter China
proposal: The text recommends giving more intelligence support to the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, including more resources, secure facilities and clearances for some private experts, to help with export controls.
quote: Provide additional support for such economic and supply chain–focused agencies as the Department of Commerce.

title: Freeze CIA hiring at the start of the new administration
proposal: The text recommends choosing a CIA Deputy Director who does not need Senate confirmation and can act immediately, including halting all current hiring.
quote: This includes halting all current hiring to prevent the “burrowing in” of outgoing political personnel.

title: Halt CIA programs that conflict with the President's agenda
proposal: The text recommends that new CIA leaders get briefings on all activities and immediately stop any program or operation they find inconsistent with the President's agenda.
quote: If senior leadership finds any program or operation to be inconsistent with the President’s agenda, the Director should immediately halt that program or operation.

title: Require CIA foreign liaison to follow State Department policy
proposal: The text recommends making clear that the CIA's relationships with foreign services must follow, not contradict, policy set by the President through the State Department.
quote: It must be clear that the CIA’s liaison relationships overseas must follow and not contradict those set at the policy level

title: Replace leaders of CIA directorates and mission centers
proposal: The text recommends that the President tell the CIA Director to hire or promote new people to lead the agency's directorates and mission centers.
quote: The President should instruct the Director to hire or promote new individuals to lead the various directorates and mission centers.

title: Broaden CIA recruiting and shift staff away from headquarters
proposal: The text recommends widening CIA recruitment, speeding up onboarding, moving resources away from headquarters, and hiring more private-sector experts into senior jobs.
quote: significantly broadening recruitment, expediting onboarding practices, and shifting resources away from headquarters

title: Move some CIA directorates out of Virginia
proposal: The text recommends permanently relocating some CIA directorates, such as Support and Science and Technology, out of Virginia, and possibly opening campuses outside the D.C. area.
quote: permanently moving various directorates, such as Support and Science and Technology, out of Virginia

title: Stop CIA spending on 'social engineering' activities
proposal: The text recommends that the CIA Director quickly move resources away from activities the text describes as promoting divisive ideological or cultural agendas.
quote: the Director should divert resources from any activities that promote unnecessary and distracting social engineering

title: Change CIA promotion rules and senior-rank requirements
proposal: The text recommends rewarding creativity and risk-taking in promotions and requiring language, technical, field or overseas experience to reach senior (GS-14 and above) rank.
quote: mandate that all CIA employees acquire, as a condition of securing senior (GS-14+) rank, additional or enhanced language skills

title: Consider using military capabilities for covert action
proposal: The text recommends that the President consider whether the Defense Department's full set of capabilities should be used to support covert actions.
quote: the President should consider whether DOD’s complete set of capabilities should be used to support potential covert actions.

title: Place covert action experts in key national security posts
proposal: The text recommends identifying transition team members experienced with covert action and placing them in key NSC, CIA, ODNI and DOD positions.
quote: identify individuals on the transition team who are familiar with the implementation of covert action with a view to placing them in key NSC, CIA

title: Conduct a 60-day review of all covert action programs
proposal: The text recommends that the NSC review all current covert action findings within 60 days, independent of the agencies running them, and then possibly change, cancel or add findings and cut bureaucracy.
quote: task the NSC’s Senior Director for Intelligence Programs with conducting a 60-day review of any current covert action findings

title: Let the DNI handpick front-office leaders
proposal: The text recommends that the DNI personally choose qualified, cleared people for front-office leadership jobs such as chief of staff and heads of legislative affairs and communications.
quote: The Director should handpick qualified, properly cleared personnel for front-office and

title: Require senior intelligence officers to accept reassignment every two years
proposal: The text recommends requiring senior intelligence officers to sign mobility agreements so ODNI and CIA leaders can move them within the intelligence community every two years if needed.
quote: Senior officers should be required to sign mobility agreements that allow ODNI and CIA leadership to move them within the IC every two years

title: Explore 'up or out' promotion rules for senior intelligence ranks
proposal: The text recommends studying added requirements for promotion to top ranks and exploring "up and out" rules starting at GS-14/15 levels in some fields.
quote: explore concepts such as “Up and Out” beginning at the GS-14/15 levels and above for some fields

title: Use buyouts to shrink intelligence agency staff
proposal: The text recommends finding areas of bloat and working with OPM on voluntary separation buyouts to shrink ODNI and CIA staff and reduce duplication.
quote: The IC should evaluate areas of bloat and underperforming cadre and work with OPM on authority for voluntary separation buyouts.

title: Remove intelligence employees who abused their positions
proposal: The text recommends that the DNI and CIA Director use their legal authority to remove employees who abused positions of trust, noting concern about people retiring before investigations end.
quote: remove IC employees who have abused their positions of trust

title: Audit past politicization and abuse of intelligence
proposal: The text recommends that the President direct the DNI and Attorney General, through inspectors general and the analytic ombudsman, to audit past politicization and abuse of intelligence.
quote: to conduct a further audit of all IC equities of past politicization and abuses of intelligence information

title: Revoke clearances of ex-intelligence chiefs who speak publicly without approval
proposal: The text recommends immediately revoking the security clearances of former senior intelligence officials who discuss their work in the media without approval from the current director.
quote: The President should immediately revoke the security clearances of any former Directors, Deputy Directors, or other senior intelligence officials

title: Fire or prosecute suspected leakers and strip pensions if convicted
proposal: The text recommends that ODNI and the CIA fire or refer for prosecution employees suspected of leaking, with loss of pension for those found guilty.
quote: The ODNI and CIA should fire or refer for prosecution any employee who is suspected of leaking information, and penalties should include the removal of pension benefits

title: Rescind Garland guidance limiting leak investigations of media records
proposal: The text recommends that the Justice Department use all its tools to investigate leaks and cancel Attorney General Garland's guidance limiting access to records of leaks to reporters.
quote: should rescind damaging guidance by Attorney General Merrick Garland that limits investigators’ ability to identify records of unauthorized disclosures

title: Hire more counterintelligence and security staff
proposal: The text recommends that intelligence agencies prioritize hiring more counterintelligence and security personnel to help stop leaks.
quote: The Director and IC must prioritize hiring additional counterintelligence and security personnel to assist in this effort.

title: Require political neutrality training for intelligence staff
proposal: The text recommends stronger training on political neutrality, including a required professionalism course in all National Intelligence University degree programs.
quote: including a mandatory course on professionalism and repercussions for abuse in the execution of duties in all degree programs at the National Intelligence University

title: Keep FISA Section 702 and let Congress weigh reforms
proposal: The text describes Section 702 surveillance of foreigners as an essential tool and recommends Congress review a 2023 privacy board report to decide whether reforms are needed.
quote: Congress should review the PCLOB’s upcoming 2023 report to help it determine whether any reforms or codification of recent administrative changes

title: Tougher penalties for intelligence leaks aimed at domestic political targets
proposal: Among possible FISA reforms, the text lists stiffer penalties and required investigations when intelligence leaks target domestic political figures.
quote: Stiffer penalties and mandatory investigations when intelligence leaks are aimed at domestic political targets

title: Tighter controls on intercepts that capture domestic political figures
proposal: Among possible FISA reforms, the text lists tighter controls on lawful surveillance that also picks up communications of domestic political figures.
quote: Tighter controls on otherwise lawful intercepts that also collect the communications of domestic political figures

title: Ban politically motivated use of intelligence powers
proposal: Among possible FISA reforms, the text lists an explicit ban on using intelligence authorities for political purposes.
quote: An express prohibition on politically motivated use of intelligence authorities

title: Increase accountability of DOJ and the FISA court
proposal: Among possible FISA reforms, the text lists changes to make the Justice Department and the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court more accountable.
quote: Reforms to improve the accountability of the Justice Department and the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court

title: Apply the Hatch Act to former officials who keep clearances
proposal: The text recommends that former senior intelligence officials who keep a security clearance remain subject to the Hatch Act's limits on political activity after leaving government.
quote: former high-ranking intelligence officials who retain a clearance should remain subject to the Hatch Act after they leave government

title: Bar intelligence agencies from monitoring domestic 'disinformation'
proposal: The text recommends prohibiting intelligence agencies from monitoring what is called domestic disinformation.
quote: The IC should be prohibited from monitoring so-called domestic disinformation.

title: Expand intelligence sharing with allies countering China, such as the Quad
proposal: The text recommends considering ad hoc or semi-formal intelligence-sharing arrangements with nations countering China, such as the Quad, rather than a blanket expansion of Five Eyes.
quote: a future conservative President should consider what resources and information-sharing relationships could be included in an ad hoc or quasi-formal intelligence expansion

title: Close loopholes in the Foreign Agents Registration Act
proposal: The text recommends examining and fixing gaps in the Foreign Agents Registration Act, with the Attorney General, to combat Chinese economic spying.
quote: to combat China’s economic espionage, authorities and loopholes in the Foreign Agents Registration Act

title: Brief more congressional committees on the China threat
proposal: The text recommends that intelligence agencies give more intelligence to a broader set of congressional committees to explain China's threat.
quote: Broader committee jurisdictions should receive additional intelligence from IC agencies as necessary

title: Expand the National Counterintelligence and Security Center's role
proposal: The text recommends using an executive order or changes to the Counterintelligence Enhancement Act to strengthen NCSC's role in counterintelligence strategy, policy and outreach, without creating a new agency.
quote: a future President and DNI should amplify NCSC’s authorities and roles with respect to counterintelligence strategy, policy, outreach, and governance

title: Give the FBI more resources and authority for counterintelligence
proposal: The text recommends giving the FBI significantly more resources and legal authority to serve as the lead operational counterintelligence agency.
quote: At the same time, the FBI requires significant additional resources and legal authorities

title: Cover foreign spying at universities in counterintelligence law
proposal: The text recommends updating the Counterintelligence Enhancement Act to include foreign espionage targeting universities.
quote: The CEA should be updated to include foreign espionage efforts aimed at universities.

title: Restore national security advisory boards for universities and business
proposal: The text recommends bringing back the National Security Higher Education Advisory Board and the National Security Business Alliance Council, led by NCSC, the FBI or both.
quote: Reinstitution of the National Security Higher Education Advisory Board and the National Security Business Alliance Council should be prioritized

title: Focus the counterterrorism center on tasks no one else does
proposal: The text recommends focusing the National Counterterrorism Center on integration work and not on analysis that duplicates the FBI and CIA.
quote: should not use personnel and resources for redundant analyses that duplicate the work of such other IC entities as the FBI and CIA

title: Prioritize long-term strategic analysis and dissenting views
proposal: The text recommends signaling demand for strategic intelligence through the priorities framework and Daily Brief, and implementing the ombudsman's recommendations on objectivity and dissent.
quote: The incoming DNI should also emphasize implementing the recommendations in the Ombudsman’s report

title: Require sharing cyber threat intelligence within 48 hours
proposal: The text recommends an "obligation to share" policy so cyber threat intelligence goes to the public or targeted groups within 48 hours, with exceptions reported to Congress.
quote: the IC must adopt an “obligation to share” policy process, including the capacity for “write to release” intelligence products

title: Build real-time auditing to track access to shared intelligence
proposal: The text recommends creating a real-time auditing system that flags unauthorized access so sensitive intelligence can be shared more widely.
quote: a robust real-time auditing capability that electronically flags unauthorized access

title: Reform classification and reduce officials who can classify
proposal: The text recommends tighter definitions of what must be classified, far fewer officials allowed to classify information, more accountability and a simpler system.
quote: More stringent policies to effect significant reductions in the number of Original Classification Authorities (OCAs).

title: Create a faster, automated declassification process run by ODNI
proposal: The text recommends a faster, largely automated declassification process run by ODNI, using tools like AI and cloud services.
quote: an ODNI-run declassification process that is faster, nimbler, default-to-automated, and larger-scale should be a priority

title: Fund declassification modernization with its own budget line
proposal: The text recommends exploring dedicated funding for declassification technology, such as its own budget line item.
quote: establishing a budget line item specifically for the modernization of declassification

title: Invest in protecting undercover officers' identities
proposal: The text recommends more resources and training so intelligence officers can work undercover despite modern digital surveillance.
quote: An incoming Administration will need to double down on resourcing and training so that members of the IC will have the expertise

title: Study and suspend burdensome parts of Executive Order 14086
proposal: The text recommends an immediate study of Executive Order 14086, which set privacy safeguards for signals intelligence tied to an EU data deal, and suspending provisions that unduly burden intelligence collection.
quote: Executive Order 14086 and suspend any provisions that unduly burden intelligence collection

title: Tie intelligence sharing with the EU to resolving data privacy rules
proposal: The text recommends telling the EU that continued intelligence sharing depends on resolving the trans-Atlantic data privacy dispute within the President's first two years.
quote: the continued sharing of intelligence with EU member states depends on successful resolution of this issue within the first two years

title: Narrow the President's Daily Brief and review who receives it
proposal: The text recommends keeping the President's Daily Brief focused on the President, with much narrower distribution, and reviewing the list of recipients during the transition.
quote: During the transition, the future National Security Advisor, along with the DNI, should conduct a review of current PDB recipients

title: Use non-CIA briefers and house all Daily Brief staff at ODNI
proposal: The text recommends considering briefers from intelligence agencies other than the CIA and locating all Daily Brief staff and production at ODNI.
quote: the entirety of the PDB staff and production should be located at ODNI

title: Require half of the National Intelligence Council to be non-CIA
proposal: The text recommends that at least 50 percent of the National Intelligence Council come from outside the CIA, and that its chair come from another major intelligence agency.
quote: require that non-CIA officers comprise at least 50 percent of the NIC’s membership

title: Make the intelligence community's IT chief a core DNI staff member
proposal: The text recommends making the Intelligence Community Chief Information Officer a primary member of the DNI's staff.
quote: An incoming Administration should appoint the ICCIO as a primary member of the DNI staff

title: Speed up post-quantum encryption across government
proposal: The text recommends immediate reviews of progress toward quantum-resistant encryption and revising the 2035 goal in a national security memo given the size of the threat.
quote: post-quantum encryption at a minimum for IC and Defense systems but preferably throughout the government

title: Focus intelligence research on hard problems, not private-sector work
proposal: The text recommends that IARPA and the CIA's Science and Technology directorate focus on hard technology problems and avoid duplicating private-sector work like AI research.
quote: The Intelligence Advanced Research Projects Activity (IARPA) and S&T should focus primarily on challenging technology problems.

title: Task the President's Intelligence Advisory Board with long-term advice
proposal: The text recommends that the President's Intelligence Advisory Board and Intelligence Oversight Board give independent advice on long-term national security issues.
quote: These entities should be tasked with giving independent, informed advice and opinion concerning major matters of national security

title: Reject adding new centers and layers to ODNI
proposal: The text recommends keeping ODNI small and rejecting calls from outside groups or Congress to add new centers and layers.
quote: calls by outside entities or Congress to add new centers and layers should be rejected

title: Integrate intelligence and military space programs
proposal: The text recommends that intelligence agencies and DOD integrate space assets, explore joint programs, and use their authorities together for space defense and offense.
quote: Fully utilize unique Title 10 and Title 50 authorities to execute space defense (and offense) strategies jointly.

title: Build space intelligence alliances beyond the Five Eyes
proposal: The text recommends that intelligence agencies support space alliances with like-minded partners beyond the Five Eyes nations.
quote: the IC should support building international alliances with like-minded partners beyond the Five Eyes intelligence-sharing nations

title: Refocus space intelligence on threats in orbit and commercial tools
proposal: The text recommends that intelligence agencies invest in tracking threats already in space, share more with DOD, and use commercial space capabilities.
quote: The IC must therefore refocus and invest in methods that will enable it to characterize accurately the threats that already exist in space
